title: Define eval sensitivity, sampling strategy, and scalable rollback playbook for Optimize
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the product requirements for a sensitivity-driven evaluation and scalable rollback playbook for the Optimize product. The goal is to provide deterministic acceptance gates, tiered rollback actions, and a repeatable promptset sampling strategy so that model changes can be deployed safely across hosted, dedicated, and private customers.

Background & motivation:
We have frequent model variant rollouts (quantized variants, kernel-level changes, and small prompt-engineering adjustments) that produce non-obvious regressions in long-tail prompt cohorts. Current canary rules rely on single-metric thresholds and manual triage, resulting in delayed rollbacks or over-reacting to noisy signals. This PRD proposes a multi-signal sensitivity approach that ties actionable thresholds to clear rollback actions and automates the early-warning and escalation flow.

Goals:
- Define a stratified promptset sampling matrix covering core cohorts + long-tail usage.
- Specify regression thresholds per-signal and per-cohort that map to concrete actions (investigate, pause rollout, full rollback).
- Create A/B criteria with statistical test choices and minimum sample sizes for rapid canaries.
- Design a staged rollback playbook that scales from traffic-shift pause to automatic fallback to a safe model variant.
- Provide acceptance criteria and observability signals to unblock SRE/eng automation.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement the automation (ENG tickets will follow). It defines thresholds, sampling, and work flows.

Users & stakeholders:
- Primary: product/platform teams running Optimize rollouts.
- Secondary: SRE, model ops, enterprise customers with strict SLAs.

Out-of-scope for this phase:
- Per-customer SLA negotiations.
- Changes to underlying serving runtime kernels.

Success metrics:
- Detectable regressions during canary window with >= 90% precision (decrease false alarms compared to current by 40%).
- Time-to-rollback reduced by 30% for high-impact regressions.
- 95% of rollouts adhere to defined staged playbook without manual override within 6 weeks of rollout adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Formalized promptset sampling: cover 3 primary cohorts (intent-stable core, edge-case long-tail, enterprise-specific) with defined sizes and derivation rules.
Regression thresholds defined for each signal type (quality, latency, token-cost, hallucination rate) with numeric thresholds and confidence windows.
A/B test criteria and statistical tests documented (two-sided proportion z-test or bootstrap for non-normal metrics) with min sample sizes computed for target MDEs.
Rollback playbook enumerated with clear action mapping: monitor -> investigate -> pause shard -> rollback variant -> postmortem.
Runbook links and dashboard mockups provided for SRE/Platform to implement automated detection and actioning rules.
Product sign-off from PM, Eng lead, and SRE lead recorded in comments before moving to ENG implementation backlog.
promptset_sampling: Sampling matrix: (1) Core cohort: top 25 intents by volume, 2k samples aggregated over 7 days; (2) Long-tail cohort: stratified random sampling across low-frequency intents, target 3k samples over rolling 14 days, with forced inclusion of known brittle prompts; (3) Enterprise cohort: customer-provided sentinel prompts + synthetic paraphrases, min 500/customer per canary. Each sample annotated with metadata (traffic segment, model variant, latency SLA class).
regression_thresholds: Quality: delta in primary eval metric (weighted utility) > 3% absolute regression with p<0.05 across core cohort => investigation required.
Long-tail quality: any cohort-level failure mode > 7% regression or new failure class discovered by heuristic detectors => pause rollout for cohort/page.
Latency: 95th percentile increases > 40ms for hosted small-latency routes OR > 20% relative increase for enterprise SLAs => pause scaling and investigate.
Token-cost: per-request token cost increase > 10% on median cost across production routes => flag for cost rollback review.

Hallucination/unsafe outputs: any statistically significant increase (p<0.01) in targeted safety violation signals or customer-reported incidents => immediate rollback to safe variant and Incident response.
ab_criteria: Minimum sample size: compute per-route based on baseline metric variance; default min N=1,500 responses per arm for general-purpose routes; N=500 per arm for targeted enterprise canaries.
Statistical test: prefer two-sided z-test for proportions (safety/acceptance pass rates). For continuous metrics (latency/cost), use bootstrap CI on medians with 95% CI robustness checks.

Stopping rules: require at least two consecutive daily checks meeting pass criteria before escalating to full rollout; early stop for harm if failure crosses critical thresholds (see regression_thresholds).
Multiple comparisons: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across cohorts and metrics to control alert volume.

Traffic allocation template: start 2% traffic to variant B, if pass at day 2 -> 10% at day 4, if pass -> 50% day 7, final 100% by day 14 pending no signals. Adjust cadence for enterprise per contract.
rollback_triggers: Immediate rollback: any increase in safety violations (targeted detectors or customer safety hook) with FDR-adjusted p<0.01 triggers automatic rollback to prior pinned variant.
Automated pause: if weighted utility metric regresses >3% on core cohort with p<0.05, shift new traffic to baseline and notify incident owner for 1-hr triage window.
Escalation path: if automated pause persists >24 hours without mitigation, auto-escalate to SRE on-call and PM/Eng for hotfix or rollback decision.
Soft rollback: for long-tail-only regressions, cut rollout to exclude affected cohorts (cohort-based routing) but continue general rollout while fixing specific failure modes.
Manual override: authorized stakeholders (SRE lead, Eng manager, PM) can trigger manual rollback; actions must be logged and reasoned for postmortem.
rollout_plan: Canary phases described above in ab_criteria. For private deployments a mirrored canary policy runs within customer VPCs using dry-run traffic and signal collection without user-visible changes; enterprise rollouts require PM sign-off at 10% step. The plan includes a 2-week pre-rollout dry-run using synthetic promptsets for each major variant.
monitoring_signals: Weighted utility (primary quality metric) per cohort and overall
Safety detector counts and rate per 10k responses
Per-request token cost median and 90th percentile
Anomalous drift signals from embedding-distance regression checks
notes: Spoke with Eng (Diego) 2026-03-04: Eng requested clearer definitions for long-tail cohorts; added forced inclusion of known brittle prompts.
SRE feedback 2026-03-08: prefer automatic pause window to be 1 hour to avoid oscillation; adjusted acceptance criteria accordingly.
Action: follow-up ENG spike to prototype automated cohort-exclusion routing (ENG-1842) to be scheduled in next sprint.
